newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cooperating with Japan in assault case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cooperating with Japan in assault case.

text.p: The United States said on Thursday it was concerned and was cooperating closely with Japanese officials in the alleged sexual assault by a U.S. sailor against his Japanese girlfriend in Japan.

"We take any incident like this very seriously," said a senior Pentagon official when asked by reporters if Wednesday's incident could harm U.S.-Japan relations at a critical time for American military basing in that nation.

"We are investigating it very seriously. We are in almost hourly contact with our Japanese interlocutors. We are closely coordinated in terms of how we proceed," said the official, who asked not to be identified.
The American petty officer remained under arrest at Yokosuka, the main U.S. naval base in Japan, on suspicion of beating and sexually assaulting his Japanese girlfriend in his quarters at the base.

No formal charges were immediately filed in the incident, which could cause new tension in Washington-Tokyo relations after the widely publicised 1995 gang rape of a Japanese schoolgirl on Okinawa by three U.S. servicemen.

"As you know, we have put in place new training provisions in Japan about cultural issues and how important it is to be good neighbours. This is our goal," the Pentagon official told reporters on Thursday.

The case could not have come at a worse time both for Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, who is battling to ensure the future of U.S. military bases in Japan, and Defence Secretary William Cohen, who makes his first visit to Japan next week.

It became public on the day that Hashimoto submitted a bill to parliament that would forcibly extend leases on some privately owned land occupied by the bases on Okinawa, home to more than half of the 47,000 U.S. troops in Japan.
The Okinawa rape case, for which three U.S. servicemen are serving jail terms, set off a campaign by local authorities which want the bases closed by 2015.
At stake are plots of land owned by 3,000 anti-bases activists who are refusing to renew the contracts. Another 29,000 landowners have agreed to renew their leases.
Police said the 21-year-old woman had told them the couple had dated for about eight months and her injuries happened during a drunken quarrel early Wednesday morning.
Yokosuka Deputy Police Chief Satoshi Nakajima told Reuters the woman said her 27-year-old boyfriend grabbed her during the argument and then dropped her on a bed.
She bounced off the bed and fell on the floor, breaking her collarbone, he quoted her as saying.
"Apparently, this is not a case of rape," Nakajima said. "The results of the medical examination of the victim show no evidence of rape."
Police were treating the case as one of assault only.
